column4: An isometric building sprite for a late-1990s camp tycoon game in the style of the reference image: 2:1 isometric pixel art seen from the south-west, the same pixel size, palette, weathered textures and soft top-left light as the reference, a small dark shadow on the ground under it. The object stands alone on a flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) background, no ground tile, no text, no border. The object: a big 1970s Czechoslovak village self-service grocery shop (Jednota samoobsluha), three times the size of the reference building: a long single-storey building with a flat roof and a thin concrete edge, a long band of big shop windows showing green shelves of goods inside, a glass double door in the middle under a small flat canopy, a long red sign board along the top of the facade without letters, grey-beige plaster with rain stains and a crack, crates of empty bottles stacked by the wall, a bicycle, a wooden bench and a red ice-cream freezer by the door.

An isometric building sprite for a late-1990s camp tycoon game of exactly the building in the reference image: 2:1 isometric pixel art seen from the south-west, the same pixel size, palette, weathered textures and soft top-left light as the reference, a small dark shadow on the ground under it. The object stands alone on a flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) background, no ground tile, no text, no border. The same building seen from behind: turned round, the same view angle and size, its long back wall now facing down to the left where the front was, plain grey-beige plaster with rain stains, a wide grey steel delivery door with a small concrete step, a brown wooden staff door with a little brass bell beside it, one small barred window, flattened cardboard boxes leaning on the wall; the short side wall on the right, plaster with a rusty drainpipe; the same flat roof with its thin concrete edge. No sign board, no shop windows, no canopy on this side.

Pixel-art texture in the style of 1990s Build-engine games (Duke Nukem 3D, Blood, Redneck Rampage): a digitized photograph crudely retouched by hand by a 1996 game artist, flat even lighting, no glow, no bloom, no depth of field, no soft shadows, chunky pixels, a limited muddy palette, low saturation, slightly grimy and imperfect, hard edges, no readable text, no logos, no border, no watermark, no people, no hands. A flat orthographic straight-on view, no perspective, filling the whole 16:9 canvas edge to edge: The front facade of a 1970s Czechoslovak village self-service grocery shop (Jednota): a long band of big shop windows with green metal shelves of bread, bottles and tins seen through the glass, a glass double door with a steel frame in the middle, a plain empty red sign board along the top, grey-beige plaster with rain streaks under the window sills, a dark plinth along the bottom. No sky, no ground, no roof, only the wall.

Pixel-art sprites in the style of 1990s Build-engine games (Duke Nukem 3D, Redneck Rampage): digitized and crudely retouched by hand, flat even lighting, chunky pixels, a limited muddy palette, low saturation, seen straight on from the front. A sprite sheet: 10 separate objects in one row from left to right, each one whole, all at the same scale, with wide gaps of background between them so none touch. The background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere, no cast shadows, no table, no text, no labels, no letters, no border, no watermark. Every object is drawn big and simple so it still reads when it is shrunk to sixteen pixels tall: plain shapes, bold dark outlines, flat fills of two or three colours. The objects, left to right: a round brown loaf of rye bread; three long crescent bread rolls in a paper bag; a long red salami; a glass bottle of milk with a green foil cap; a glass jar of pickled gherkins; a brown glass beer bottle with a green label; a chocolate ice cream bar on a stick; a chocolate bar in a red wrapper; a head of green cabbage; a white bar of soap in a blue paper wrapper.
